assets.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram. Asset type: wide scientific architecture illustration for the EvoHarness GitHub README. Create a new polished diagram in the SAME visual language as the stellarator figures viewed in this conversation: white background, large dark navy sans-serif lettering, softly tinted blue/teal/lavender/amber rounded rectangles, thin vivid colored outlines, clear blue arrows, restrained subtle gradients, ample whitespace. Landscape 16:9. No photographic elements, no 3D effects, no equations, no small footnotes.
Exact title: "How EvoHarness evolves a CVRP solver"
Exact subtitle: "Implemented today: capacity constraints and distance minimization"
Architecture: left blue box "LLM writer" with smaller "Edits Python + C". Center large pale teal container labeled "Docker sandbox · one CPU" enclosing two side-by-side boxes. First: "Candidate solver" with smaller "Construction + ruin / recreate". Second: "C local search" with smaller "Relocate · swap · 2-opt". A blue arrow connects writer into candidate; bidirectional arrows between candidate and C engine denote search iterations. Center-bottom inside sandbox a tiny schematic depot with 3 colored customer routes (illustrative only). A short line inside sandbox bottom reads "3–6 seconds per instance".
Right amber box OUTSIDE sandbox labeled "Trusted evaluator" with smaller lines "Coverage + capacity" and "Recompute route distance". Arrow sandbox -> evaluator labeled "Routes".
Along bottom a lavender box "Selection + feedback" with smaller lines "Train / validation · repeat near ties" and "Optional reviewed memory". Arrow evaluator -> selection -> looping back to LLM writer. Separate small blue box lower right "Held-out audit" with text "Private split + 30 s validation"; arrow from selection to this box, no arrow from held-out audit back to writer. Very bottom concise caption: "Programs evolve; model weights stay fixed."
Use exactly the named labels, legible text, and keep evaluator visibly outside sandbox. Do not imply time windows, route-count optimization, challenge readiness, or established superiority of memory.
assets.role: Implemented CVRP workflow; conceptual illustration, not numeric evidence.

assets.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram. Asset type: wide architecture illustration for EvoHarness research report and README.
Create a NEW scientific diagram visually matching the generated CVRP image and the existing VMEC++ illustrations: white background, bold dark navy sans-serif type, softly tinted blue, teal, lavender and amber rounded boxes, thin vivid outlines, clear directional arrows, subtle gradients, generous whitespace. Landscape 16:9, crisp readable labels. Use simple route/clock icons. No plots of results.
Exact title: "A hybrid optimizer for the VRPTW challenge"
Exact subtitle: "Proposed next architecture · not implemented yet"
Main left-to-right pipeline with 4 large boxes:
1 lavender: "LLM evolution" with two lines "Propose small operators" and "Ruin · repair · decomposition"
2 teal: "Trusted VRPTW core" with lines "Time-window feasibility" and "Fleet reduction + local search"
3 blue: "Matched-budget evaluation" with lines "Fixed instances + seeds" and "Vehicles first, distance second"
4 amber: "Promotion gate" with lines "Repeated proxy gains" and "Transfer to larger instances"
Arrows 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4. A clear feedback arrow from box 3 curves down and returns to box 1, labelled "Verified outcomes + isolated memory".
Below on the right, a separate teal box "Long-run solver portfolio" with text "Multi-seed search on XLTW"; arrow from Promotion gate down to this box. Then arrow to amber "Independent validation" with text "Official checker + solution archive".
Below on the left a pale blue box "Freeze the core" with two lines "Evolve policies behind a small interface" and "Keep feasibility and scoring outside candidate code".
Bottom caption exactly: "Hypothesis: better search policies can transfer from cheap proxies to XL instances."
Make the phrase "not implemented yet" prominent in subtitle. Avoid claiming a competition win, proven transfer, implementation completeness, or availability of an official checker today. No extra text.
